summary: Not a corpus gap. The operator has a dedicated procedure, 'CIP-014/LSPG CIP-014 Physical Security Procedure V8.pdf' (document_number LSPG-ADM-CIP014, internal jurisdiction, authority_tier 3), that substantively implements CIP-014-3 end to end and even carries its own requirements-traceability appendix (section 5.1) mapping each CIP-014 requirement/Part to the procedure section that addresses it. The reranker (candidate_links.build_links, DEFAULT_THRESHOLD=0.5) proposed zero candidates for any of the 17 Part-level requirements despite this document existing and being retrievable by ordinary semantic search (compliance_search surfaced it on the first query, scores ~0.013-0.017). This is a retrieval/reranker recall failure across an entire standard, not a documented no_operator_document finding.

findings.reason: Procedure §3.1 'Risk Assessment', §3.1.4 explicitly states the 30/60-month subsequent-assessment cadence matching R1 Part 1.1 verbatim; also named in the procedure's own traceability appendix (isection-7a80d3bd98433c322111) as 'Section 3.1.4'.
Procedure §3.1.5: 'LSPG shall identify the primary control center that operationally controls each site...' — matches R1 Part 1.2 verbatim; traceability appendix names 'Section 3.1.5'.
Traceability appendix maps R2 Part 2.1 (unaffiliated verifying entity selection) to 'Section 3.2.2' of the same procedure.
Traceability appendix maps R2 Part 2.2 (90-day verification window) to 'Section 3.2'.
Traceability appendix maps R2 Part 2.3 (60-day response to verifier recommendations) to 'Section 3.2.4.1'.
Traceability appendix maps R2 Part 2.4 (NDA/confidentiality protections for the third-party verifier) to 'Section 3.2.5'.
Traceability appendix maps R4 Part 4.1 (unique facility characteristics) to 'Section 3.4.2.1'; procedure §3.4 is the threat/vulnerability evaluation section per the appendix's R4 row.

Traceability appendix's R4 row continues into Part 4.2 (prior-attack history) under procedure §3.4.x; table was truncated by the read tool's max_chars before the exact sub-id, but the parent section §3.4 is confirmed to exist and cover R4.

Same §3.4 threat/vulnerability evaluation section covers all of R4's Parts per the appendix's structure (4.1, 4.2 confirmed present; 4.3 falls in the same subsection run, not independently re-verified due to read-length truncation — flagged for a follow-up compliance_read at a higher offset).
Procedure §3.5 'Physical Security Plan', §3.5.1: 'LSPG shall develop and implement a documented physical security plan' — directly implements R5's core duty.
§3.5.2: plan developed/approved within 120 calendar days of third-party verification — matches R5 Part 5.2's timing requirement.

§3.5.3.1-3.5.3.6 enumerate the plan's required content (timeline, resiliency measures, security controls, threat response, law-enforcement coordination, evolving-threat evaluation) — matches R5's attribute list.
Same §3.5 content list (law-enforcement coordination at §3.5.3.5) addresses R5 Part 5.4.

Procedure §3.6 'Physical Security Plan Unaffiliated Third-Party Review', §3.6.1: review covers both the Threat/Vulnerability Evaluation (§3.4) and the Physical Security Plan (§3.5) — matches R6's scope.

§3.6.2 names the qualifying criteria for the unaffiliated reviewing entity (CPP/PSP certification, ERO approval, government/law-enforcement expertise) — matches R6 Part 6.2's reviewer-qualification requirement.
§3.6.3: review completed/documented within 90 calendar days of plan approval — matches R6 Part 6.3's timing requirement.
§3.6.4-3.6.5: 60-day response to reviewer recommendations and confidentiality protections — matches R6 Part 6.4.

method_note: Searched via mcp__portal-compliance__compliance_search (jurisdiction=operator) with queries targeting risk assessment, third-party verification, physical security plan, and third-party review vocabulary; confirmed section text via mcp__portal-compliance__compliance_read. Did not modify the store or any relationship_assertions — this is a recall-miss finding for a future retrieval/reranker task to act on, per §P2's own instruction not to change DEFAULT_THRESHOLD in this task.
recommendation: This is a retrieval-pipeline defect, not a corpus gap: candidate_links.build_links never proposed the LSPG CIP-014 Physical Security Procedure as a candidate for ANY of CIP-014-3's 17 requirements despite a purpose-built, requirement-by-requirement traceability appendix existing in the same document. Worth a follow-up task investigating why the projection/rerank stage failed to surface this document at all for this standard (embedding/index gap, standard-id mismatch in the projection query, or a population-construction bug specific to CIP-014-3's identity resolution) — distinct from the empty_population structural non-reach diagnosed for the other five dead standards.
